_sources.12: Form 1040-NR (2025), line 12 is itemized deductions 'or, for certain residents of India, standard deduction' — a Chinese student gets 0; Instructions for Form 1040-NR (2025), Line 12.
_sources.16: TY2025 Tax Table (Instructions for Form 1040 (2025), Tax Table, from the engine's extracted table params/2025-tax-table.json): single, taxable income $3,000 to $3,050 -> tax $303.
_sources.1a: Instructions for Form 1040-NR (2025), 'Amounts Exempt Under a Treaty', example 2 (all wages on the W-2): report W-2 wages MINUS the treaty amount on line 1a and the treaty amount on line 1k — $8,000 - $5,000 = $3,000.
_sources.1k: Form 1040-NR (2025), line 1k 'Total income exempt by a treaty (from Schedule OI, item L)' = $5,000 (Schedule OI entry: China, Article 20(c), $5,000).
_sources.25a: Form 1040-NR (2025), line 25a: Form W-2 box 2 withholding.
_sources.37: Form 1040-NR (2025), line 37 = line 24 ($303) minus line 33 ($300) = $3 owed.
_sources.treaty_wage_exclusion: U.S.-China treaty, Article 20(c): a student resident of China is exempt on income from personal services performed in the U.S. 'in an amount not in excess of 5,000 United States dollars' per taxable year (treaty text, irs.gov/pub/irs-trty/china.pdf; params/2025-treaties.json).

description: NR-001: Chinese F-1 student (second calendar year in status), campus wages $8,000 all reported on the W-2 (no Form 8233 split), $300 withheld. The China treaty Article 20(c) $5,000 personal-services exemption is claimed ON the return: line 1a carries only the taxable $3,000 and line 1k carries the exempt $5,000 (Schedule OI). No standard deduction for nonresident aliens. Small amount owed.
